anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 74 Greek; no published English version was used for wording.

choices.why: ‘Man has become like vanity’ (Ἄνθρωπος ματαιότητι ὡμοιώθη) is LXX Psalm 143:4, cited by English numbering as Psalm 144:4.
‘Sealed with the Holy Spirit’ (κατεσφραγίσθαι τῷ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι) is cited as an allusion to Ephesians 1:13 (compare Ephesians 4:30).

choices.english: through the Holy Spirit, who is his own
choices.why: ‘Through the Holy Spirit, who is his own’ (ὅ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ): the neuter relative agrees with Πνεῦμα; Cyril means the Spirit is the Son’s own Spirit.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing ‘rich in’] righteousness (δικαιοσύνη); thus we are sharers (κοινωνοί) of divine nature; Christ is housed (ἐνοικίζεται) in us through the Holy Spirit. Lemma: if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you. The Lord Jesus Christ has been raised by the Father, life being worked (ἐνεργουμένης) about his flesh through the Holy Spirit, which is his (ὅ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ); for that he himself made alive (ἐζωοποίει) his own temple (ναός), he says to the Jews ‘Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it’; so even if said to be raised by the Father, still he himself was the raiser (ὁ ἀνιστάς) through the Holy Spirit; for all God-befitting things (θεοπρεπῆ) are worked from Father through Son in Spirit; Christ will therefore raise our bodies too. Lemma: as many as are led by God's Spirit, these are sons of God. Those living by spirit are led by Spirit, through being sealed (κατεσφραγίσθαι) with the Holy Spirit, freed from slavery in law and letter (γράμμα), crossed over to freedom, witnessed by the Spirit of adoption (υἱοθεσία) that they are sons of God, and in that Spirit have cried out ‘Abba, the Father’. Lemma: if we suffer-with (συμπάσχομεν), that we be glorified-with. The good is achieved not [without toil (πόνος)], but toil on great hopes for the saints; nothing earthly promised, but glory unmeasured (ἀμήρυτος) and participation (μέθεξις) in things above mind and word. Those overlooking earthly things worthy of the highest prizes (γέρα); those who toiled before in courage and endurance (ὑπομονή) will enjoy crowns in incomparable superiorities; toil for virtue falls short (μειονεκτεῖται) of later honours. He says glory of saints since the just will shine out in due times as the sun, come into honour, glory and incorruption (ἀφθαρσία) when their body is changed (μεταβληθῆναι), as Christ was transformed (μετεμορφώθη) on the mountain. Lemma: the eager expectation (ἀποκαραδοκία) of creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God. Ἀποκαραδοκία = hope, expectation and watching of the outcome of things; creation awaits the revelation of the children of God, not itself knowing what will be — how or whence? — but because by the ineffable economies (οἰκονομίαι) of God reshaping (μεταρυθμίζοντος) all to the better, to this the end will come; the children of God being remoulded (μεταπλαττομένων) as into glory from dishonour, from corruption to incorruption, i.e. those achieving the approved life, creation itself will be re-tuned (μεθαρμοσθήσεται) for the better; the godly Peter (θεσπέσιος) does not let us doubt, saying ‘new heavens and new earth and his promises we await’. Lemma: to vanity (ματαιότης) creation was subjected. Vanity here he calls those living in vanity, i.e. in fleshly mind; of whom fitly said ‘Man was likened to vanity’; and indeed also that [continues next unit].
pass_b_english: …with righteousness. For in this way we are partakers of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4), since Christ makes his dwelling in us through the Holy Spirit.
But if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you (Romans 8:11).
Our Lord Jesus Christ was raised by the Father, life being worked in his flesh through the Holy Spirit, who is his own.
For he himself gave life to his own temple, as he shows when he says to the Jews, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19).

So even if he is said to have been raised by the Father, it was nonetheless he himself who raised it up through the Holy Spirit; for every work befitting God is worked by the Father through the Son in the Spirit.
Christ, then, will also raise our bodies from the dead.
For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God (Romans 8:14).

Those who live by the spirit are the ones who are also led by the Spirit, because they have been sealed with the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 1:13), set free from the slavery that lies in law and letter, and passed over instead into freedom, and because the Spirit of adoption bears them witness that they are sons of God and that in that same Spirit of adoption they have cried out, “Abba, Father” (Romans 8:15-16).
If indeed we suffer with him, so that we may also be glorified with him (Romans 8:17).

The good is not achieved [without toil], but for the saints the toil rests on great hopes. For nothing earthly has been promised them, but glory without measure and a share in what lies beyond mind and speech.

For those who disdain the things of earth are worthy of the highest rewards, and those who have first toiled with courage and endurance will enjoy crowns of a preeminence beyond compare; for the toil spent on virtue falls short of the honors that follow.

He speaks of the glory of the saints because in due time the righteous will shine like the sun (Matthew 13:43), having come into honor, glory and incorruption when their bodies are changed, just as Christ was transfigured on the mountain (Matthew 17:2).
For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revealing of the sons of God (Romans 8:19).
“Eager expectation” means hope: the looking for and watching out for how events will turn out.

Creation does await the revealing of the children of God, not because it knows in any way what is to come—how could it, or from where?—but because, by the hidden dispensations of God, who reshapes all things for the better, matters will come to this end.

For when the children of God—that is, those who have achieved a life of good repute—are refashioned, as it were, from dishonor into glory and from corruption into incorruption, creation itself too will surely be changed for the better.
On this point the inspired Peter does not let us doubt, when he says, “We await new heavens and a new earth, and the things he has promised” (2 Peter 3:13).
For creation was subjected to vanity (Romans 8:20).
Here he calls “vanity” those who live in vanity, that is, in a fleshly mind. Of them it might be said quite fittingly, “Man has become like vanity” (Psalm 144:4), and indeed also that…

reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Staged new row, reviewed clause by clause against the PG Greek. (1) ὅτι γὰρ αὐτὸς … ἐζωοποίει … λέγει: 'For to show that' made the saying Christ's purpose; now 'For he himself gave life to his own temple, as he shows when he says'. (2) μαρτυρεῖσθαι … ὅτι τε εἰσὶν υἱοὶ Θεοῦ, καὶ … διακεκράγασιν stays inside the διὰ τό causal chain; the split-off sentence 'They receive the witness…' is folded back in ('and because the Spirit of adoption bears them witness that they are sons of God and that … they have cried out'). (3) οἱ γὰρ … ὑπερορῶντες: γάρ restored ('For') and 'disdain' replaces the weak 'look past'; ἐν ἀσυγκρίτοις ὑπεροχαῖς is 'of a preeminence beyond compare', not 'in honours beyond compare'. (4) πρὸς τοῦτο ἥξει τὸ τέλος: 'matters will come to this end' replaces 'its end will come to this', which wrongly made the end creation's own. (5) British spellings (honour, dishonour) changed to the book's American spelling; divine pronouns lowercased to match the book. Scripture refs checked, including Psalm 144:4 = LXX 143:4.
Opens mid-sentence: δικαιοσύνην completes πλουτοῦν at the end of u06-rem-mid (‘enriched … with righteousness’, glossing Romans 8:10); the leading ellipsis marks the join.
Closes mid-sentence (καὶ μὴν καὶ ὅτι); the quotation that follows (Psalm 49:12) opens u07-open. Trailing ellipsis marks the join.
‘Man has become like vanity’ (Ἄνθρωπος ματαιότητι ὡμοιώθη) is LXX Psalm 143:4, cited by English numbering as Psalm 144:4.
2 Peter 3:13 is quoted in Cyril’s wording (καὶ τὰ ἐπαγγέλματα αὐτοῦ, ‘and the things he has promised’) rather than the standard text (κατὰ τὸ ἐπάγγελμα αὐτοῦ); rendered as Cyril has it.
οὐ[κ ἄνευ πόνου]: the bracketed words are an editorial restoration in PG; the brackets are kept in the reading text.
‘Sealed with the Holy Spirit’ (κατεσφραγίσθαι τῷ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι) is cited as an allusion to Ephesians 1:13 (compare Ephesians 4:30).
‘Honor, glory and incorruption’ may echo Romans 2:7, and ‘when their bodies are changed’ 1 Corinthians 15:51-52; both uncertain, not cited inline.
‘Through the Holy Spirit, who is his own’ (ὅ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ): the neuter relative agrees with Πνεῦμα; Cyril means the Spirit is the Son’s own Spirit.
PG page numbers 215 and 216 and Khazarzar page marker 18 are not text and are omitted.
